glossary.kind: what an object is: group, forum, post, …
glossary.op: one typed change a kind declares
glossary.delta: one writing of an op — signed, epoch-stamped, in a log
glossary.fold: sequenced or commutative: how the log orders it
glossary.ego: who is acting: a PRINCIPAL, identified by a public key, never a kind. What it must be to the target is one of owner, member or arc.
glossary.facet: ops several kinds share, in a reserved op-id band
glossary.part: a constituent object a kind is made of — declared at both ends, `part_of`
glossary.relation: an edge between objects, projected from an op
glossary.halves: whether BOTH endpoints declare their own half of a relation, or only one. `one` means the far end never writes anything, so the edge is a claim it cannot refuse and need not know about. Orthogonal to `writtenIn`.
glossary.writtenIn: whose log carries the declaration: the source's, the target's, or NEITHER (a Contact channel is a pipe, not an endpoint). With halves=one this names which end made the claim — for `assigned_to` it is the project, and the person named never consented.

mls.policy: RFC 9420, with application policy per RFC 9750 §5 — docs/membership-through-mls.md. Pinned against the code by pacific-core/src/icd.rs::the_mls_section_matches_the_code.

floor.setBy: creation; raised only, by the owner

mls.legacyOwner: leaf 0 while the owner extension is absent; remove and handover refused until it is set

applicationPayload.summary: Every application message carries the Delta with its author's signature, and a Node verifies it before storing it and again before folding it; the author is the signer, not the MLS leaf (A-10 part 1; SEC-35; NC-21, CS-32). Awaiting Ralph's approval as an ICD change.

cbor.1: envelope: the Delta's canonical bytes, unchanged, so every delta id stands
cbor.3: sig: Ed25519 by the author over delta_sig::authorship_payload(group_id, author, delta_id)

applicationPayload.refused: a payload with no signature, or one that does not prove its author, is quarantined with a reason naming the signature and never stored; a stored row whose signature fails makes its object noncompliant, named
applicationPayload.history: A payload may also arrive in a `history` bundle (mls.intro.kinds.history) from the object's admitter that sealed the joiner's Welcome. The joiner stores it only if the sender is that admitter, the delta id is the hash of the envelope, the envelope's group is the object, and the A-10 signature verifies for the object; then by what the row is. A spine row is the owner's. A base.publishProfile row (a card) is stored when its author is on the object's roster now: a card is standing, not an event, and its subject is its author, whose A-10 signature it must carry (a card names no one else). Every other row (a post, and the rows beside it: reacts, receipts, votes, retracts, membership records) is stored on the admitter's signed bundle: that its author was a member when it was written rests on the admitter's signature, and the joiner does not check it. A payload that fails is refused and named; one already held is ignored. A stored payload keeps the admitter as its provenance ("via admitter") and folds as any other; a card received directly later supersedes a bundled one by gen, per author, as the profiles fold orders any two (O-75; mdr/arc-history.md; pdr/history-review.md; Ralph, 29 Sep: "Use the MLS welcome history package, delivered by the arc")

intro.summary: What is sealed to one member's intro mailbox, outside every group epoch: sealed (seal.rs) to the intro_tag of that member's contact bundle, which any holder of the bundle can seal to, so a kind whose sender matters proves its sender itself. The plaintext is CBOR; a map whose `kind` is "history" is a history bundle, and anything else is a Welcome's payload

welcome.summary: An MLS Welcome to one object, with the object's kind, owner and Arc (handshake::IntroPayload). Its sender is proved by the Welcome: the joined group's roster and GroupContext

history.summary: A late joiner's history of one object (O-75): the rows the object's admitter holds, sent at admission to the member it admitted, and to no one else. Additive: no op, kind or Delta changes
history.from: the admitter of `object` that committed the joiner's Add, as recorded at its Welcome
history.to: the member that Add admitted, sealed to its intro key as the Welcome is

cbor.joiner: bytes: the 32-byte identity key of the member it is for; a device refuses a bundle naming another
cbor.rows: array of bytes: each an mls.applicationPayload ({1: envelope, 2: author, 3: sig}; delta_sig::seal_payload), exactly as a member received it, unaltered
cbor.sig: bytes: Ed25519 by `sender` over SHA-256("wallflowers/history/v1" ‖ 0x00 ‖ u32be len(object) ‖ object ‖ joiner ‖ sender ‖ u32be count(rows) ‖ for each row, u32be len(payload) ‖ payload)

history.order: the owner's sequenced spine first, whole and in chain order (a partial spine breaks the chain); then the other rows, newest first; then the cards
history.capSummary: bytes of the encoded bundle: what one relay blob carries once sealed (the relay's 262,144 base64 characters, less the seal's 40 bytes: a 24-byte nonce and a 16-byte tag). The spine goes whole, then the newest rows to the cap; a spine over the cap is not sent, and the admitter names it
history.carriage: one object's history is one or more bundles, each within `cap` and each signed whole on its own for the same `object` and `joiner`. The first carries the spine, whole, and the rows beside it; the cards follow in further bundles, as many as `cardsTotal` allows. A joiner checks each bundle on its own, and a row is stored at most once, whichever bundle brings it
history.cardsTotalSummary: bytes of encoded card bundles, together, for one object at one admission (2 MiB); the spine's bundle is not counted. The newest cards go first; past it nothing more is sent, and the admitter names how many cards were not sent
history.cards: the latest facets.profiles base.publishProfile row of each member on the object's roster at admission, one per member, newest first by gen, whatever epoch it was written in. A departed member's card is never sent
history.refused: whole, and named: a bundle whose signature does not verify, whose `joiner` is not this device, whose `sender` is not the committer of this device's Welcome for the object or holds no admitter role there, or over the cap. A row that fails applicationPayload.history's checks is refused and named, and the rest are stored. A bundle for an object not yet joined is held until its Welcome joins it, and refused as never admitted if none does within an hour

historyPolicy.summary: Per object, whether its admitter shares the object's history with a member it admits (the MIMI room policy's history_sharing and automatically_share; pdr/history-review.md): automatically, capped, of that object only, to that member only
historyPolicy.group: shared: a Site, by the admitter that admits to it
historyPolicy.forum: shared: a room whose admitter role the admitting Arc holds, admitted with its Site
historyPolicy.host: never: the Arc serves its items from its own fold, and its members are Arcs
historyPolicy.conversation: never: a DM admits no one
historyPolicy.contact: never: a tether admits no one
historyPolicy.cards: shared with a Site's or a room's history: each current member's latest card, sent with it by the same admitter to the same member, within the same total
historyPolicy.posts: shared with a Site's or a room's history (Ralph, 29 Sep: "Use the MLS welcome history package, delivered by the arc"): its posts and the rows beside them (reacts, receipts, votes, retracts, membership records), newest first to the cap, after the spine in the spine's bundle (mls.intro.kinds.history.order); the cards go in their own bundles. A retraction is newer than the row it withdraws, so it travels whenever that row does, and a withdrawn row stays withdrawn
historyPolicy.otherwise: never: only an object whose admitter admitted the member

conformance.asserts: Every op declared by ObjectType::ops() appears here with a matching opId, authority and fold, and every message here maps to a declared op. Adding an op to a reducer without giving it a graph clause fails the build. The KIND LIST is derived from ObjectKind::ALL by an exhaustive match, so a new object kind does not compile until it has a channel here or a stated reason for having none — SystemType had a reducer, an author door and no channel until 15 Sep 2026, and nothing failed.

member_of.note: the edge itself comes from the roster; this op only writes its role property

owns.note: and invalidate the outgoing owner's owns edge at the same instant

publishes.note: an Arc Node and the object it serves at a slug. The Arc is a principal (principals.arc), and it holds an identity Group like any other Node — so its half belongs there, the way `group.joinedObject` is the person's half of `member_of`.

subscribes_to.note: subId is not the target; resolve it from the folded state

missingHalf.note: Reciprocity is required; this relation declares one half. The far endpoint names NO KIND — the arg is an opaque id — so which kind needs the op is itself unruled.

sold_through.note: A Site's sale (T-3; ASSURANCE 30 Sep): the Transaction's half names the Site and the Thing (transaction.setSite); the Site's half is its own listing of that Thing (group.publishListing, `site` 1, by the owner or an admin). The WallFlowers system node sells only what the Site listed.

membership.summary: who is in it, recorded by the MLS doors beside the commit that makes it true

base.memberJoined.summary: Someone joined the roster. A RECORD of the MLS Add, written by whoever COMMITTED it, alongside it (membership-through-mls.md §10.3) — at a public door that is any member, which is why the authority is anyMember. A record is a claim about the ratchet tree, never the operation: MembershipLog::divergence compares the two, and group_author refuses to write this op — only the Add door does.

rel.name: member_of
rel.note: opens the tenure: valid_at = at

base.memberLeft.summary: Someone left, or was removed. A RECORD of the MLS Remove, never the Remove itself (membership-through-mls.md §10.3): written by the leaver before proposing their own removal, or by the owner before committing one. ANY member may author their OWN departure — leaving never needs the owner online, because any member commits the leaver's proposal (§7) — and the owner may author anyone's. left vs removed is DERIVED from the author, never a wire arg, so it cannot be forged. `reason` is optional and from a closed set (requested | lost_device | inactive | conduct | other); an unknown value is malformed. Commutative because only the owner may write the sequenced spine. group_author refuses to write this op — only the leave and remove doors do.

rel.name: member_of
rel.note: closes the tenure: invalid_at = at. The edge survives; a departure is an interval that ended, not an edge that never was

base.ownerHandover.summary: The owner hands the object to another member. A RECORD of the GroupContextExtensions commit that moves the owner extension (membership-through-mls.md §9): written by the outgoing owner, on the spine, at the last epoch they own. The commit is what makes it true, and the spine follows the owner epoch by epoch (§10.2). The ONE membership op that is the owner's alone, because it is the only one that changes who may write the spine. Required before an owner may leave: an ownerless object can never accept another sequenced delta, so it would be frozen forever. group_author refuses to write this op — only the hand-over door does.

rel.name: owns
rel.note: and invalidate the outgoing owner's owns edge at the same instant

base.claimSpent.summary: A kiosk claim was spent on an Add (A-3, SEC-A1; D-53, Ralph 27 Sep): the sha256 of its nonce, never the token, and who it admitted, written by the admitter beside base.memberJoined. The first per claim holds, so a claim admits once however many copies race, and the spend survives the admitter's restart. The reducer holds the author to the owner or an admitter; role-valued ego waits on A-10 part 2.

claim.summary: sha256 of the claim's 16-byte nonce, 64 hex (pacific_core::claim::Claim::spent_key)

member.summary: the identity key the claim admitted

share.summary: the claim's `a`: the Artifact's share id, 20 characters of abcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz23456789

publication.summary: its public address, and the member that serves it

base.publish.summary: Give this object a PUBLIC ADDRESS and name the member that serves it. Not a fourth visibility level: visibility grades reach through the mesh in hops, and an HTTP reader is not at a distance in the mesh, they are outside it — so publication is its own facet and the two are set independently. The publisher must already be in the roster (a non-member could never fold the state it claims to serve), which also makes publishing visible and revocable: remove the member and the serving stops. NOTE this op is a ONE-WAY DOOR in a way the visibility dial is not — once served over HTTP a projection is cached by parties outside the protocol, and base.unpublish cannot retract it.

edges.note: the Arc named here serves this object. Written in the OBJECT, by its owner — the Arc declares nothing, which is the missing half.

base.unpublish.summary: Withdraw the public address. Clears BOTH the slug and the publisher: leaving the slug would keep the object claiming an address it no longer serves, and a later publisher would inherit a name the owner may not have re-chosen. Carries no args — the absence IS the instruction. This stops the publisher serving; it does not un-publish what the web already read.

ratify.summary: propose, vote, close — every object accepts a ratification

ratify.propose.summary:
Open a question the group decides together. `payload` is the DEFERRED content a passing close commits — a decision text in this slice, generalising to an inner delta the close activates — and `rule` is how it passes: 0 consent (it passes unless an eligible member REJECTED, so approve, abstain and silence are all fine), 1 owner (the owner approved). The rule rides the PROPOSAL rather than sitting in object configuration, because what a decision was taken under has to stay legible from the log years later, and a setting can be changed after the vote. There is no id argument: a proposal IS the (author, gen) of this delta, which is what makes it unforgeable — only its author can mint one in their own name — and it is the pair `ratify.vote` and `ratify.close` carry back as target_author/target_gen. The proposer implicitly approves their own proposal; an explicit later ballot of theirs replaces that. Solo, an electorate of one, collapses the whole three-op dance to "author the delta".

DOCUMENTED 16 Sep 2026, ON THE WIRE SINCE M4, and the gap is the point. RATIFY is a base op-group `Coordinator::deliver` recognises AHEAD of a type's own op table and `Coordinator::ratify_state` folds — never `T::reduce`, so the domain never learns about voting — which means no `ObjectType` declares these three, and for the whole of M4 nothing here did either: three ops accepted on every object, in no op table and in no channel, found by `harness/objects/cases.py` rather than by anything that fails. `icd.rs` now holds every channel against `coordinator::RATIFY_OPS`.

ratify.vote.summary: A ballot on a proposal: 1 approve, 2 reject, 3 abstain. Abstain has a code of its own because a RECORDED non-vote is not silence — under consent both let the proposal pass, but only one of them is evidence that the member saw it. `target_author`/`target_gen` name the proposal exactly as `forum.vote` names a message, the same (author, gen) pair, because a proposal id IS its propose's (author, gen). LWW per (proposal, voter) by this delta's own `gen`, so changing your mind is a later ballot rather than a retraction. A ballot from a member who has since LEFT stops counting: `ratify_state` filters the OR-set by the CURRENT roster, deliberately unlike `Coordinator::state`, which exempts membership ops so that a departure can still record itself.

ratify.close.summary:
A FROZEN close (membership-through-mls.md §10.4): it names its `electorate` and the exact `ballots` (delta ids) it counts, each a JSON array of hex in one text arg, and a closed proposal is judged from the close alone — no later removal or handover can re-decide it, and an owner-approval proposal is judged by the owner who closed it. A listed ballot not yet held leaves the outcome Pending; a listed ballot on another proposal or from outside the electorate makes the close inert; a ballot held but not listed is reported (RatifyState.unlisted). A close WITHOUT the two args is LEGACY and re-reads the current roster — the defect this ended. 

Freeze the tally. Owner-sequenced, and RATIFY's only serialization point: two closes racing on different in-flight tallies must not produce two answers, so a close rides the hash-chained spine where the owner assigns (epoch, seq) and a fork is refused. It carries NO outcome — pending|passed|failed is DERIVED at read time from the frozen roster × the frozen ballots × the proposal's rule, for the same reason a wallet balance is never stored. What the freeze does hold is the ELECTORATE: membership and roles go on changing, and a decision has to keep meaning what it meant when it was taken. A close naming a proposal this device has not folded is inert rather than an error, because the propose may still be in flight; a ballot that lands after the close is a documented simplification of this first slice and not a solved consistency claim (`Coordinator::ratify_state`).

THE OP IS IMPLEMENTED — proven end to end over real MLS and a real relay by `pacific-core/tests/m4_ratify.rs`, four devices converging on one outcome — and `status: implemented` says that. THE EPISODE IS NOT WRITTEN YET: nothing projects a ratified decision into the graph today (`Node`'s ratify doors never touch the projection sink), so the `episode` clause here is the CONTRACT, not a description of the projector. The field has two readers who read it two ways — this document's preamble defines it as the projector's state, while `harness/objects` refuses any op marked `specified` as unrunnable — and of the two available errors, a harness asserting on green that a ratification cannot run is much the worse, because it is a false claim about a feature four devices already converge on. So the status follows the code and the projector gap is stated here instead.

ratify.note: EVERY kind, without exception — `deliver` has no kind whose objects refuse a ratification, so a channel that dropped these would be claiming one that does not exist. This list was the ten kinds that existed when it was written and did not grow with the taxonomy; `icd_matches_every_op_table` checks it per channel, which is what caught that.

base.setVisibility.summary: How far this object may travel: private | connections | network. Defaults to private, so an object from a build predating visibility can never travel further than intended.

vocabulary.network: anyone the mesh reaches; for an event or post, also its Site's public Face

visibility.note: On event and post since 2.3.0 (NC-139, Ralph 30 Sep: "A is good"). THE DEFAULT IS PER KIND: a place with none is private, as before; an event or a post with none is `network`, because before 2.3.0 every event and post a Site created was public on its Face (O-48), and an absent value must not withdraw them. face_items hydrates an event or post into its Site's Host only at `network`; `private` and `connections` are members only and never reach the Face, and a later change to either withdraws the item there.

location.summary: where an object is — a reference, not a coordinate

base.setLocation.summary: The common location facet: JSON LocationSource, Fixed{point:{lat,lng}} or Stream{access}. This is the op that makes an object render as a map pin.

base.clearLocation.summary: Unset the location. The node survives; it just stops being placeable.

roles.summary: what one member of an object IS to it — its standing
roles.note:
Standing is a facet, so any kind may carry it. Since 25 September it is also the basis of AUTHORITY: an op declaring `ego: "role:x"` is checked against this state, so the facet must reach any kind whose ops use one.

NOT `treasury`, though it was briefly listed here. A Treasury's roster IS the money's roster — everyone on it is a treasurer, and the way you are not trusted with the money is not being on the object at all. It was added speculatively with role-valued ego and `icd_matches_every_op_table` refused it: the document claimed ops the kind does not declare.

base.setRole.summary: Role of an EXISTING roster member. Does not add anyone.

member.summary: the member's identity key — the standing is an overlay on the roster, and a standing granted to someone not in the MLS tree is refused

role.summary: owner | admin | member | viewer | guest | admitter. An admitter may add a member and record the Add, and nothing else: the Arc's always-on node, granted by a founder, revoked with base.clearRole at its position (A-3; D-53, Ralph 27 Sep) settler | seller | buyer: on a Transaction only, each set once in its mint and fixed for its lifecycle (T-2, T-3; Ralph 30 Sep).

base.clearRole.summary: Take a member's standing away. They stay on the roster: the MLS tree is the roster and a role is an overlay on it.

member.summary: the member's identity key — the standing is an overlay on the roster, and a standing granted to someone not in the MLS tree is refused

parts.summary: the objects this one is made of — its rooms, its comments, its Treasury, its Host, its sub-groups — each in a role

base.setPart.summary: Name an object this one is made of, in a role. The part is its own GroupObject with its own MLS roster and its own name; this op writes only the edge. The part's half is `base.setParent`; mint writes both. Took over base.setForum's wire id, 26 September 2026: composition is general, and there is one way to write it.

rel.name: part_of
rel.note: who is IN the part stays the part's own roster; this edge says only that it is part of the target, and in what role

role.summary: what the part is for: room, comments, treasury, host, … Not empty.

choice.summary: role `room` only, refused on any other role. An admitter adds a claim's visitor to its room parts whose choice is the claim's `c`; when none carries `c`, or the claim has none, to its room parts without a choice. A part in any other role is joined on every claim.

base.clearPart.summary: Detach the part. The part object, its log and its roster are untouched. Detaching one never attached fails loudly.

parent.summary: the other half: the part naming the object it is a part of, so the edge can be walked from the child
parent.note: Reciprocal of the `parts` facet, ruled 25 September 2026, and on every kind since 26 September 2026: composition is general — rooms, comments, a Treasury, a Host and a sub-group are each a part with a role. Written at mint, when the parent's owner is the sole member and owner of the part, so one principal authors both halves with no race.

base.setParent.summary: Name the object this one is a part of, and in what role. The parent's half is its `parts` op; both are written by the same mint.

edges.note: the child half — the same triple the parent declares, written where it can be walked from

base.clearParent.summary: Detach. The parent is untouched; it clears its own half with its `parts` op.

backlink.summary: this object declaring its own half of a relation another object asserted
backlink.note: `group.setAffiliation` is this mechanism, group-only, and predates it. A kind that is not a Group had no way to write its half at all, which is why `created` and `happens_at` were one-sided. Added 25 September 2026 with the reciprocity ruling; band 0xF009. NOT put on `group`, because two ways to write one fact is two sources of truth — a Group writes its halves with setAffiliation.

base.setBacklink.summary: Declare this object's half: the object at the other end, and which relation.

vocabulary.venue: happens_at — the Place this happens at, declared BY the Place

edges.note: the created object naming its creator — the half group.setAffiliation {rel: created} asserts
the Place naming an event held there. Until now a Place had six ops and none could record one.

base.clearBacklink.summary: Withdraw this side's half. The far end keeps its own.

profiles.summary: each member's own card in this object: a name and optionally a picture
profiles.note: O-77, ICD 2.1.0. Band 0xF00A. The card's key is its signer's, never a field, so a card names no one else.

base.publishProfile.summary: The author's own card in this object: a name and optionally a picture. Per-author LWW by gen. The subject is the author; a card names no one else.

card.summary: JSON: `displayName`, not empty; optionally `photo`, a still image in standard base64, with `photo_mime`, image/webp, image/png or image/jpeg (both or neither), ContactCard's own picture fields; any other field is refused. At most 16384 bytes of UTF-8; refused, never truncated.

gen.summary: per author, the highest wins

about.summary: each member's own words about themselves in this Site: a bio and a few links
about.note: W-98 Members ('a developed, site scoped bio and info'). Band 0xF00B. Ruled out: base.publishProfile (displayName and photo only, republished from the self record by O-77, the same on every Site); group.setProfile (the owner's, the group's own identity). The info half is the member's answers (facet questions).

base.publishAbout.summary: The author's own bio and links in this Site, published by the member themselves as base.publishProfile is; every member of the Site reads it. Per-author LWW by gen; the subject is the author, never a field. Empty bio and no links clears.

bio.summary: plain text, at most 4096 bytes of UTF-8; refused, never truncated; empty clears

links.summary: JSON array of at most 3 https URLs, each at most 2048 characters; absent is none

gen.summary: per this group's log, the Lamport generation; the highest (gen, author) that counts wins

view.about: {<member key>: {bio, links, gen}}: members on the roster only

questions.summary: questions the Site's owner or admins put to its members, free text or a choice of options, and each member's answer
questions.note: W-98 Members ('Site owner/admin can define free questions and multiselect polls'). Band 0xF00C. A question has no id: it IS the (author, gen) of its base.defineQuestion, as a proposal is its ratify.propose. Ruled out: the ratify facet (one payload, approve/object/abstain, no options, no free answer); forum.vote (up/down on a message).

base.defineQuestion.summary: Put a question to the Site's members. It counts while its author is the owner or holds admin, as group.editFace's writes do.

text.summary: at most 1024 bytes of UTF-8, not empty

options.summary: JSON array of 2 to 24 distinct labels, each 1 to 80 characters; absent for a free question

multi.summary: 1: several options may be chosen; 0 or absent: one. Only with options

free.summary: 1: a free-text answer is taken (with options, as well as them); absent is 1 without options, 0 with

gen.summary: per this group's log, the Lamport generation; the highest (gen, author) that counts wins

max.summary: with multi, at most this many options may be chosen (node.cyp3.xyz's OFFER: 4); 2 to the options' count; absent is no cap below the count

hint.summary: a line shown with the question, at most 200 bytes of UTF-8; absent is none

textMax.summary: the free-text answer's cap in bytes of UTF-8, 1 to 4096 (node.cyp3.xyz's SEEK 180, IMAGINE 500); absent is 4096. Only where the question takes free text

base.retireQuestion.summary: Close a question to new answers; it and its answers stay in the view, marked retired.

gen.summary: per this group's log, the Lamport generation; the highest (gen, author) that counts wins

base.answerQuestion.summary: The author's answer to one question. Per (author, question) LWW by gen; a later answer replaces it, an empty one clears it. Refused on a retired question.

text.summary: at most the question's textMax (else 4096) bytes of UTF-8; only where the question takes free text

choices.summary: JSON array of option indexes, distinct and in range; at most one unless multi, and at most the question's max

gen.summary: per this group's log, the Lamport generation; the highest (gen, author) that counts wins

view.questions: [{author, gen, text, options, multi, free, retired, answers: {<member key>: {text, choices, gen}}, tally: [count per option]}]: questions whose author counts, oldest first; answers from members on the roster only

group.summary: An organisation, team, or (shape=individual) a person's identity record.

group.setProfile.summary: Name + shape of the identity record. shape in {individual,team,organisation,community}; individual makes it a Person node.

group.setPresence.summary: Whether this party is reachable on Pacific. Routing, not meaning.

identityKey.summary: required when kind is onPlatform: a 32-byte IdentityKey

event.setLineup.description: The event view gains `acts`. Each act's name, picture and links are its profile's own card, read from the Site view's `profiles`; an act whose profile this device does not hold is shown as unresolved, never dropped. event.setProfile's `lineup` (newline names) stays readable for old events only; a client that writes acts stops writing lineup. Written by the owner or a co-host (base.setRole admin on the Event; Ralph 30 Sep), checked at write and at fold against THIS Event's roles and roster; a revoked admin's writes stop counting. THE PERFORMER'S CONSENT is its own half of performs_at: a person on their self record, an organisation on its own group, by group.setAffiliation {rel: performs_at, peer: the Event}. An edge is declared in both nodes, so an act is `confirmed` only to a reader who holds the performer's half (the performer, the organisation's members, and the public where the organisation's Host carries it); a person's self record is private, so to others their act reads unconfirmed. THE PUBLIC COPY (face_items, host.hydrate) carries an act only when it is confirmed from the writer's own view; an unconfirmed person's act stays inside MLS. An organisation's act confirms publicly through its own Host. Judged by the folded roles, as group.editFace is: revoking a co-host withdraws every edit of theirs, the photos they added included.

post.setProfile.summary: The words. A Post's op 0, and the only op that can change what it says. `form` is article | link | image | pdf — a DISCRIMINATOR, not a hint: without it the four are told apart by guessing at the other fields (a link is "a body that looks like a URL", an image is "a banner with no body"), and a lane cannot render four shapes it cannot name. Absent folds to `article`, so a post from a build predating the field folds as the thing it almost certainly was. `link` is a link post's destination, a pdf's document, or an image's full-size source, and the fold REFUSES one on an article — a destination on an article is a contradiction, not a spare field.
post.setProfile.description:
OWNER-ONLY, because a Post is one author's statement — a Viewer who could edit it would be able to put words in the author's mouth on the author's own spine. SEQUENCED, so two edits from the same owner on two devices resolve by position rather than by arrival.

`title` is required and `body` is not: a Post may be a headline. The reverse would make an untitled post unfindable in a list, which is the same rule every other kind applies to its name.

Refused rather than clamped, because silently shrinking someone's image is a worse answer than telling them it did not fit. Enforced in the REDUCER, so the rule binds a patched peer as well as our own client.

The log is append-only and every member already holds it, so nothing here deletes anything — pretending otherwise would be a lie about what a distributed log can do. What a retraction does is stop the object CLAIMING to be readable: the fold sets a tombstone and the UI shows that instead of the words.

Owner-only. A Viewer who could retract could silence the author.

ANY-MEMBER, and therefore COMMUTATIVE — the spec invariant is that a broadcast op cannot be owner-gated before it propagates. This is one of the two ops a VIEWER may author, and together they are the whole of what the Viewer role means.

Keyed by author, so reactions do not stack: setting a new emoji replaces the old one and an explicit empty string clears it. The reducer checks roster membership itself, because any-member is not no-member — a delta from someone off the roster is noise.

system.define.summary: What this System is: the human name, the connector id the app dispatches on, and what it is currently pulling.
system.define.description:
Owner/sequenced. `connector` is the dispatch key ("music.ra", "art.artrabbit") and is how `Node::system_for_connector` finds where to hydrate INTO, so a connector never has to remember which group it wrote to last time. `scope` is free text OWNED BY THE CONNECTOR ("area=218;window=14d") and is opaque to the core on purpose — a new source must not need a core change to describe what it is fetching.

Op id 0, as the catalogue has always declared. Ids 1–9 stay RESERVED for the connector op-group (addField · setConnector · bindCredential · …) that remains unbuilt; hydration took 10 so that building those later needs no renumbering.

scope.summary: Optional. Opaque to the core — the connector owns its grammar.

system.hydrate.summary: One item as its source produced it. `key` is the dedup key, `rev` the LWW key, `withdrawn` a tombstone rather than a deletion.
system.hydrate.description:
Any-member/commutative, per-key LWW by `rev`. `payload` is the source's own JSON kept VERBATIM: the System that wrote it owns its shape and every reader parses the same bytes, which is what lets a new connector ship without a core change. Capped at 16KB and REFUSED rather than truncated — a silently clipped payload would parse on some devices and not others.

A STALE REPLAY IS A NO-OP, not a rejection: two devices hydrating the same source race constantly, and a loud reject on the loser would poison a fold over a difference that does not matter. Equal revs keep what is held, so the fold is a function of the delta SET and not of arrival order.

`withdrawn` is a TOMBSTONE. The news that a listing was cancelled has to travel the same paths the listing did, so it is state rather than absence — the discipline `contact.publishListing` already uses.

key.summary: The source's stable id, e.g. `ra:event:166016`. THE dedup key — re-fetching the same listing produces the same key.

payload.summary: The source's own JSON, verbatim. At most 16384 bytes.

fetchedAt.summary: When the connector observed it, epoch ms. Provenance, not validity.

rev.summary: The source's revision, monotone per key. The LWW key.

withdrawn.summary: Optional 0|1. The source withdrew it — a tombstone that travels.

treasury.summary: A shared treasury and the attestations over it. Its own roster, so a member of the body need not be a member of the money — the case shared-wallets.html §104 named as the one that would justify promoting it out of group.

treasury.setPolicy.summary: Open a shared treasury and fix how it may be released. `bands` is the schedule, one rung per line as `ceiling|rule|quorum` with `*` for the open top band — the rule belongs to the AMOUNT, because one threshold is either too brittle to buy timber or too loose to spend half the wallet. Quorum counts the electorate; the rule's threshold counts only the ballots that expressed a preference, and collapsing the two lets a pair of members awake at 3am move everything. `account` is a NAME ("Triodos •2291"), never a credential, and is deliberately NOT projected: it is addressing material for someone else's system, which is the ground group.setPresence is excluded on. `cooloffHours` is ADVISORY — a pure reducer has no clock, so a breach surfaces as a divergence rather than a rejection.

treasury.recordDeposit.summary: Money arrived. An OR-set row keyed by `reference` under a single-writer discipline — event.recordSale keyed by `pi`, exactly — so a redelivered delta is idempotent rather than a second deposit, and a late-joining member converges from any delivery order. Amounts are integer MINOR UNITS, never floats, for the reason geo stores coordinates as fixed-point e7. Nobody votes on money arriving. Reaches the graph as an EPISODE: a dated financial fact, not entity state.

treasury.attestSettlement.summary: A member states that they moved funds in an account Pacific never sees. TESTIMONY, NOT PROOF — the fold is pure and cannot verify it, and that is why `proposal` names the RATIFY decision it discharges. Its ABSENCE is meaningful rather than missing: legitimate below the petty band, and a divergence above it. The delta is accepted either way, because refusing it would delete the evidence of the one thing worth catching; Wallet::divergence is what has an opinion. Not embedded: an embedding is reversible, and a memo carrying an amount and a bank reference is the group.storeCredential argument in another currency.

treasury.attestBalance.summary: "The real account held this, on this date, and I am the one saying so." The anchor the derived balance is reconciled against — the balance itself is never stored, being deposits less settlements, for the reason RATIFY derives Outcome from the frozen tally rather than storing it. Per-author LWW by `at`, so two treasurers counting on different days keep separate slots and an older count never overwrites a newer one. A negative amount is legal: an overdrawn account is a fact.

note.summary: Prose with its own roster. A private notebook is a Note whose roster is one: roster size is not a kind, which is why `notebook` and `note` collapse here.

note.write.summary: Write or rewrite YOUR entry for one note. The slot is keyed (author, note), so nobody else's delta can ever land in it — which is what makes "only the author edits their own words" structural rather than a permission check. Last-write-wins by the AUTHOR's own `at`, with `text` as the deterministic tie-break, so the fold is a function of the delta set and never of arrival order. `at` rides the op because import_archive overwrites received_at with now and the envelope carries no timestamp; without it every restored note's clock collapses to restore time. `at` is BOUNDED: unbounded, one op dated 2099 would win its slot forever and silently delete every co-author's words from the rendered note.

note.retract.summary: Retract YOUR OWN entry for one note. Lands in the SAME (author, note) slot as noteWrite, so retract-versus-write is resolved by one total order and a later write by the same author legitimately resurrects the entry. A TOMBSTONE: it carries nothing forward from the entry it supersedes, because a candidate derived from current state would depend on what had already been delivered and two replicas would disagree. On a SHARED note this is a statement, never a purge — the words remain in every member's log, and the interface must say so. Removing someone else's words is a membership act, not this op.

note.comment.summary: Comment on a shared note. Keyed (author, commentId) so two members may use the same comment id without colliding. Capped at exactly post.MAX_COMMENT_CHARS — one rule in two places. Reaches the graph as an EPISODE: a dated utterance about a note, not state on the note itself.

note.react.summary: React to a note with one emoji. Keyed (author, note), so a member holds at most one reaction per note. An EMPTY emoji is the cleared state rather than a row removal: a removal would need its own tombstone to stay commutative, and the empty string already is one.

note.promote.summary: Record that a private note now has a SHARED twin, and name the object it lives in. Authored on the NOTEBOOK, so the private note knows where its twin is and the editor routes later edits there. This is the idempotency key for promotion: it must be written FIRST, so a retried share reuses the existing twin instead of minting a second note object holding the same text.

rel.name: created
rel.note: the notebook minted this note's SHARED twin. The private entry stays where it is, so this edge is the only record of where the shared copy lives — and it is what makes a retried promotion reuse the existing object instead of minting a second one.

host.summary: A Site's public copy, and the only object an Arc joins. Its roster is the owner's devices and the Arc; the group's members are not on it and the Arc is on nothing else. What is here is what is public, put here deliberately by a Delta the group can see and revoke. Built on branch host-faces as System(21) + connector wallflowers.host; promoted to a kind 25 September 2026, as Treasury and Note were.

host.define.summary: Name it. The connector string that used to make host-only ops legal is what the kind now means.

host.hydrate.summary: The public copy. Key `face` is the bundle verbatim; keys `event:<id>` and `post:<id>` are live items. Per-key LWW by rev, 16 KB each, `withdrawn` is a tombstone.
host.hydrate.description: REFUSED FROM THE ARC. ego=member admits the Arc by leaf, and the fold rejects a hydrate the publisher authored: a server may not write the page it serves. That refusal now has a name in this document — see principals.arc. A post reaches its Site's Host only at visibility `network`; the Arc serves its public page from these items (W-98 Resources; Ralph 30 Sep). When a post is retracted or leaves `network`, every key it wrote (its body chunks, its assets, its document) is written `withdrawn` (D-60: not visible, not served). No payload carries the Secret (O-79) of an item that is not `network`: the Host copy is the only way out of MLS.

subsumes.why: An overfitted precursor. It is one sale machine that only knows about EVENT TICKETS: 3,204 lines whose state machine (open → paid → fulfilled → refunded), capacity gate, dedup and redemption table are all things a Transaction GroupObject holds natively, in a log two parties and a settler can fold. The object IS the interface, so the HTTP plane that stood in for it is not needed.
subsumes.whatDoesNotSubsume: The `Rail` trait (rail.rs:83) and its Stripe implementation. Touching money needs a processor, and that stays the SETTLER's private concern — which is the point of the settler owning the object. the-payment-rail.html already ruled the shape: the interface stays open, the implementation closes. A Transaction makes the interface an OBJECT rather than an HTTP spec, which keeps that promise better than publishing routes did.
subsumes.invariantToCarry: "Pacific nets exactly the 10¢-equivalent per ticket; processing costs ride the ..." — enforced in rail.rs at money-creation time. As a Transaction it becomes a term both parties SEE before accepting, which the design already argues is P2B satisfied structurally rather than disclosed.

principals.settler: owner of the object, and `role:settler`: the Arc's settling plane (principals.arcPlanes). Mints the Transaction, holds no deal role, and writes only transaction.resolve (a dispute) and transaction.fraudSignal (stub). May NOT author the deal.
principals.seller: `role:seller`. States the terms, attests the sale.
principals.party: A seller or a buyer is a person's identity, or a Site acting through the WallFlowers system node (kind `system`), which holds the Site's seat always online: a member can buy from a Site (T-3; Ralph 30 Sep: "both sites and users can be in the transaction. you can buy something from a site. this is handled by wallflowers-system node."). In a Site's sale the Transaction names the Site (transaction.setSite) and the Site's half is its own listing of that Thing (group.publishListing with `site` 1): the system node writes the seller's ops only for a Thing the Site listed, checked at write, since no fold reads another object. The seller's seat is a Site's; a Site as the buyer is not in 2.3.1.
principals.note: Three parties, three authorities — the case role-valued ego was ruled for. The settler owning the object is what stops either party evicting the other; holding no deal role is what stops the mediator writing the deal.
principals.operator: In a Site's sale the Arc's operator holds the seller's seat (the system node) and the settler's (the settling plane): separate Nodes and seeds, so no identity holds two roles, but the mediator of a dispute is the same operator as one party (T-3, T-5; ASSURANCE 30 Sep, named for Ralph's pin row).

recordOnly.summary: Record only (T-6; Ralph 30 Sep: "record only for now"). No op charges, holds, releases or refunds money, and WallFlowers takes no fee: `amount` is what the parties agreed, paid between them outside WallFlowers. `completed` means both parties said so, not that money moved.

roles.fixed: Fixed for the Transaction's lifecycle (T-2; Ralph 30 Sep: "roles are fixed for the lifecycle of the transaction"): the settler's mint writes all three base.setRole, one principal role per member, before any other op but transaction.setSite; a base.setRole after the first non-role op, a second role for a member, and any base.clearRole are refused at write and at fold.

transaction.sourceOfTruth: The Transaction's own log (T-5, BUILD for Ralph, 30 Sep). Completion is two Deltas in it, the buyer's transaction.confirmReceipt and the seller's transaction.confirmSale, each accepted only from that role in the state that allows it. The fold derives the state; the settler writes nothing for completion and folds the same log the parties fold. The CommunityAPI's routes write a party's attestation from that party's own Node; the Arc never attests for a party.

stateMachine.silence: Completion by silence (BW-E's fix 4; T-5, BUILD's draft for Ralph to confirm): an accepted Transaction with one attestation and no dispute reads `completed` once the terms' confirmWithin has passed since that attestation's `at`, naming who attested. stateMachine.clock: Every time is its author's word, and the log shows who said what (ASSURANCE 30 Sep). The fold checks the one bound it can check the same on every replica: an op's `at` is not before the `at` of the op it answers; one that is, is inert and named. A party can still date an op late within that bound (an accept after acceptBy by their clock, a dispute inside confirmWithin); under record only the harm is to the record, and the settler reads it.

legs.summary: Pairwise-channel claims. Each is a delta in a Contact log that carries a claim about a THIRD object, because the recipient is not on that object's roster and cannot read it. The Contact log is neither endpoint of the claim — the ICD says so itself: "a Contact log is a pipe, not an entity" — so these are NOT GroupObject→GroupObject triples and are not relations. Ruled 25 September 2026. They were projected as edges (offers, identifies, invited_to, going_to); that projection put facts in the graph which live inside a pipe between two people and are invisible to the object they are about.
legs.why: You cannot write into a group you are not a member of. Every cross-boundary fact therefore travels as a message. The mechanism is necessary; calling the message an edge was the error.

RULED 16 Sep 2026: the web interior's `rsvp {event, going}` IS this op, not a new one on the Event. It cannot be an Event op — an Event's roster is the organiser and their door staff, and buyers and guests deliberately never join it (`event.rs`), so a guest is not a member of the object they are answering about and `Coordinator::deliver` would refuse their delta as Unauthorized. The answer has to ride the pairwise channel the invitation came down, and `going` is the same boolean this leg already carries.

homes.contact.publishListing: thing.setPosture {posture, price, reach, area} is the fact's real home on the Thing; this leg is a fan-out copy.
homes.contact.publishProfile: group.setProfile on the author's own identity record is the real home; this leg is a per-author LWW cache for peers who cannot read it.
homes.contact.invite: NO HOME. An Event has six ops and not one is about people — it cannot record an invitee. The leg carries the Event's title and startMs precisely because "the invitee may never see the real Event".
homes.contact.inviteReply: NO HOME. An Event cannot record an attendee, so an RSVP exists only in the channel it was sent through.

reciprocity.summary: Every relation is declared at BOTH ends: a delta in the source's log and a delta in the target's. Ruled 25 September 2026. The argument is traversal, not symmetry — a one-sided edge cannot be walked from the far end, so an object reached on its own is contextless. A member of a role-gated comments Forum who is not on the parent's roster holds a Forum that cannot say what it is the comments section OF; the spine enumerates it and the fold is silent. A person's WallFlowers is the subgraph they can walk, so an unwalkable edge is not in it.
reciprocity.model: member_of: base.memberJoined in the object, group.joinedObject in the person. One relation, two ops, one per endpoint.

principals.summary: The kinds of principal an op may require. An ego is a public key, not a GroupObject. `ego` is one of owner, member, arc, or `role:<name>` — a member holding that standing.
principals.owner: the identity in the MLS GroupContext owner extension, at the delta's epoch
principals.member: any leaf on the target's roster
principals.arc: an Arc PLANE's Node, holding a leaf in each object that plane serves — a principal that READS. One Node per plane: a keypair, a head and a spine. The fold refuses a hydrate the publisher authored, because a server may not write the page it serves.

arcPlanes.rule: one Node per Arc plane, not per object
arcPlanes.model: A plane's Node has a keypair, a head and a spine. Its spine is the chronological record of the objects it serves: the hosting plane's entries are Hosts, the settling plane's are Transactions. Each entry is already an independent MLS GroupObject with its own roster, epoch and ratchet.
arcPlanes.isolation: The spine gives it, and nothing else is needed. `chain_locator(root, g, i)` puts every index at an unrelated HKDF address, so "the store sees no stable per-account tag and cannot count an account's objects from the addresses" (spine.rs). Without the PLANE SEED the objects are unlinkable — not merely unreadable, unlinkable. Per-object keypairs would add N identities to achieve less than one seed already does.
arcPlanes.separation: Hosting and settling are different planes, so different Nodes and different seeds. A stolen hosting seed links and reads Hosts, whose contents are public by construction; it reaches no Transaction, because that spine is derived from a seed it does not hold.
arcPlanes.costsNothing: Planes are separate binaries under arc/planes/, so one Node each is one PACIFIC_STATE_DIR each — which `paths::state_dir()` already gives per process. No core change: no per-object identity, no key store, no Node::open_at.

principals.role:
`role:<name>` — a member holding that standing in the target's folded `roles` state, written by `base.setRole`. Ruled 25 September 2026, because owner|member could not express a Transaction: buyer and seller are both members, and nothing distinguished them.

IT ALSO SUPPLIES THE NEGATIVE, which is the part owner|member could not do at all. `Owner` is a SUPERSET — an owner may write everything a member may — so "the settler may not author the deal" had no expression. With role-valued ego it needs no special case: the deal ops require role:seller or role:buyer, the settler holds neither, and the check that refuses a stranger refuses the owner by the same rule. No negative authority, no exception.
principals.either: `a|b` — either principal. `owner|role:admin` is the object's owner, or a member on its current roster holding admin in its own folded `roles` state. Ruled 29 September 2026 for ICD 2.1.0 row 10, for an op the owner and an admin may both author; it is only ever commutative, since the sequenced spine takes the owner alone.
principals.enforcement: One check beside the existing owner check in `authoring::build`: resolve the author's role from the folded state the `roles` facet already maintains, and refuse if it is not the declared one. The roles facet must reach any kind whose ops use role-valued ego.
